findings.text: The _review_delivery_verdict docstring still reads 'record is this run's delivery only when all four hold' while enumerating five conditions, and the function returns six distinct condition strings (the path condition splits into 'no head-keyed record path' and 'record cannot be read'), so a reader counting conditions from the docstring disagrees with the code it documents.

_review_missing_measures iterates review['absent'], which the replaced rule only tested for truthiness, so a stored record carrying a truthy non-iterable absent (absent: true or 1) now raises TypeError instead of reading as incomplete; _review_is_complete is called from recovery_classification.py:618, obligations.py:453, recovery_repair_dispatch.py:586 and recovery_review_acceptance.py:38, so a malformed record crashes a classification pass rather than being refused. Measured at this head: _review_missing_measures({'status':'parsed','scores':{},'absent':True,'total':1}) raises TypeError: 'bool' object is not iterable, where the base rule returned False. The fleet's own writer emits a list (reckon/crew/review.py:880), so reachability needs a malformed or hand-written record.

The delivered verdict sets 'path' to the Path from _declared_head_keyed_record (typed tuple[Path, str] at recovery_review_delivery.py:104) while every refusal branch sets it to str(path), or to "" for the no-path condition, so one dict has two types under one key and a caller asking verdict['path'].exists() breaks only on the refusal arms.

CASES builds five conditions and none of them stores an unreadable record, so the 'record cannot be read' arm (_review_delivery_refusal, recovery_review_delivery.py:404) has no test that reddens if it is removed or reworded, and the fragment's claim that a corrupt file still says the record 'cannot be read' is not pinned by the gate; only the parsing half of that claim is asserted.

_read_complete_review survives the move of its logic into _review_delivery_verdict with no reader left inside the module (the verdict calls _read_review_record and _review_missing_measures directly at lines 400 and 410), and a search over reckon/ and tests/ finds only its definition and the recovery.py:200 re-export, so the file carries a second path to the completeness judgement beside the verdict's.
